health.debtValue: {pct}% of income goes to debt minimums
health.savingsValue: {pct}% of income goes to your goals
health.tip_emergency: Build your emergency fund: even $25 a week adds up. Aim for 3 months of bills.

health.explain: Not a credit score. It's how your month and your cushion look from your own numbers: emergency fund (3 months of bills = full points), debt minimums (10% of income or less = full), saving (15% or more = full) and what's left (10% or more = full). 25 points each. Emergency savings counts goals named like "emergency fund" and your Safe to Spend cushion.

steps_emergency: Open a separate savings account just for it.
Set up an automatic transfer on payday.
Use it only for real emergencies, then refill it.
steps_home: Check your credit reports free at AnnualCreditReport.com.
Ask about first-time buyer programs in your state.
If you're a veteran, ask about a VA home loan: often no down payment.
Get preapproved before you look at homes.
steps_car: Decide your total price before you go to the dealer.
Get a loan offer from your bank or credit union first.
Keep the loan short, 48 months or less if you can.
steps_business: Write down what you need to start and what each thing costs.
Keep business money in its own account.
Set aside for taxes from every payment.
Get free help from your local SBDC or a SCORE mentor.
steps_retire: If your job matches 401(k) savings, try to get the full match.
An IRA is a retirement account you can open yourself.
Start small and raise it a little each year.
